                    1          Plaintiff Google LLC (“Google”), by and through its attorneys of record, brings this action

                    2   against Defendants Yaniv Asayag and Does 1–20 (together, “Defendants”) for (1) breach of

                    3   contract; and (2) violation of California’s Unfair Competition Law (“UCL”), Cal. Bus. & Prof.

                    4   Code § 17200 et seq. Google alleges as follows:

                    5          1.      Over the past two years, Mr. Asayag has abused Google services to create fake

                    6   online listings for businesses that do not exist and to bolster them with fake reviews from people

                    7   who do not exist. Mr. Asayag has also engaged in an ongoing fraudulent “lead-generation” scheme

                    8   by selling to third parties information about consumers lured in by his fake business listings.

                    9          2.      Google provides (among other things) detailed public listings of local businesses on

                   10   Google services like Maps and Search with accompanying ratings and reviews submitted by Google

                   11   users. The authenticity of these listings and reviews is essential to businesses, their customers, and

                   12   Google. Online ratings and reviews, such as those found on Google Maps, play a crucial role in

                   13   influencing the decisions of numerous potential customers when they are searching for businesses

                   14   to engage with. Accordingly, these ratings and reviews must offer authentic information about the

                   15   business’s products and services based on users’ real experiences. Google’s policies and its

                   16   contracts with individuals who post reviews or edit business listings make these requirements of

                   17   authenticity clear.

                   18          3.      Importantly, the authenticity of these ratings and reviews is critical in ensuring the

                   19   privacy and safety of Google users who may consult such information when soliciting businesses

                   20   for goods and services. Consumers who contact a business based on its Google listing may entrust

                   21   their personal information to the business, including their names, phone numbers, addresses, access

                   22   to their homes or property, and more. Purveyors of fake profiles and reviews on Google can exploit

                   23   these innocent consumers’ trust and risk their safety by selling their personal information to third

                   24   parties as leads, thereby establishing a connection between the consumer and a third party with

                   25   whom the consumer never intended to engage or otherwise interact with. In many instances, these

                   26   third parties will take advantage of these oblivious consumers to significantly upcharge or, in more

                   27   extreme cases, out-and-out extort a consumer who is desperately seeking emergency or urgent

                   28   services.
COOLEY LLP
ATTORNEYS AT LAW
 SAN FRANCISCO

                    1          4.      For these reasons, Google employs numerous methods to prevent and remove fake

                    2   or otherwise inappropriate reviews on Google Maps and Google Search. As part of these initiatives,

                    3   Google has determined that Mr. Asayag, and other potential co-conspirators involved, are engaged

                    4   in an ongoing pattern of fraudulent conduct by selling and posting fake reviews for businesses listed

                    5   on Google Maps and Google Search, in violation of the Google’s Terms of Service and California

                    6   law.

                    7          5.      Defendants’ conduct harms consumers by giving them fake information about

                    8   businesses and obscuring genuine reviews. Internet users look to Google Maps and other Google

                    9   services to compare businesses and decide which to engage. When a business’s reviews do not

                   10   reflect consumers’ real experiences with that business, it provides members of the public with false

                   11   and inauthentic information about the quality of that business’s goods or services. Such fake

                   12   reviews also crowd out reports of consumers’ real interactions with that business, creating a

                   13   misleading picture about the business and driving out potential customers. Defendants’ conduct

                   14   harms legitimate businesses by enabling unscrupulous competitors who purchase fake reviews to

                   15   unfairly siphon customers away.

                   16          6.      Defendants’ conduct poses a risk of irreparable injury to Google by undermining

                   17   Google’s credibility with its users and by making Google Maps and Google Search less attractive
